defects.title: 304 payload reuse is turned into an incorrect shared-state no-op
defects.materiality: Both topics read the shared freshness state; stale eligibility or validators can change with no payload. The local keep-one-until-next-successful-revalidation rule also contradicts retention untouched on a successful 304. The proposed fixture would approve this inconsistency.

defects.title: Blanket offline fallback loses HTTP-cache versus application-history conditions and an age bound
defects.materiality: “Whenever offline” supplies no expiry branch and conflicts with rejecting unbounded stale use. A marker and named policy constants do not define which store is a conforming cache, what permissions apply, or when old pixels stop being displayed.

defects.title: Provider policy is reduced to rates/identity while offline exclusion and seven-day fallback are omitted
defects.materiality: A small, slow or quota-bounded offline download remains prohibited at that endpoint. Applying seven days unconditionally also loses server-header freshness conditions. These are governing conditions of the chosen primary policy.

defects.title: Resume support probes omit the representation binding needed for safe cross-version byte resume
defects.materiality: The topic explicitly shares changing tile versions. Resuming an old prefix against a newer suffix can corrupt the tile even if 206 support was demonstrated. The suggested 206/416-only oracle misses valid 200 fallback and representation changes. The 10–40 KB rationale has no captured measurement.

defects.title: Status-only rules broaden SIE and overstate 404 removal
defects.materiality: The default can continue display for unrelated authorization/request failures and terminate an otherwise useful cached tile on temporary 404. Its status fixture locks in these wrong classifications; “SIE scope unresolved” obscures a condition already in the captured source.

defects.title: A MediaWiki parser-cache TTL is attributed to mod_tile expiry
defects.materiality: The sole asserted numeric tile precedent for retention is absent. This is a consequential source-attribution error even though the final also says quotas are unresolved and the precedent is nonnormative. Hashes and grep counts cannot establish this semantic claim.
